note: Paradigm tables, written for this project.
why: The grammar corpus explains these systems in prose. Exactly one of its 626 rules is a full six-person paradigm, so a table cannot be extracted from it. These were written here instead, from the closed paradigms of standard German — the article, pronoun and adjective-ending systems are fixed, finite and checkable against any reference grammar, which is why they can be written without inventing anything. Anything that is a matter of usage rather than a closed paradigm is NOT here: it stays prose.

g-daf-a1-definite-articles-in-the-nomina.caption: Definite article
g-daf-a1-definite-articles-in-the-nomina.emphasisNote: Only the masculine changes in the accusative: der becomes den. Every other box is the same in both rows.

g-daf-a1-indefinite-articles-and-negativ.caption: ein- and kein-
g-daf-a1-indefinite-articles-and-negativ.emphasisNote: Again only the masculine changes: ein becomes einen, kein becomes keinen.

key.means: no word here — German has no plural of ein, so the plural uses kein on its own
the indefinite article, then the negative one: ein Hund, kein Hund

g-daf-a1-personal-pronouns-in-the-accusa.caption: Personal pronouns
g-daf-a1-personal-pronouns-in-the-accusa.emphasisNote: These five change in the accusative. sie, es and Sie are spelled the same in both columns.

g-daf-a1-possessive-articles-in-nominati.caption: Possessive article, nominative
g-daf-a1-possessive-articles-in-nominati.emphasisNote: The feminine and plural form is the masculine one plus -e. Only euer is irregular: it drops its second e to give eure.

key.means: lower case is "her" or "their"; capitalised is the polite "your"

g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-definite-a.caption: Definite article in all four cases
g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-definite-a.emphasisNote: The dative row is this lesson: dem, dem, der, den.
g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-definite-a.asideNote: The genitive is shown for completeness; it is taught in a later topic.

key.means: the article den, and the noun itself takes an extra -n: den Söhnen
the article des, and the noun takes -s or -es: des Sohnes, des Kindes

g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-indefinite.caption: ein- / kein- / mein-, all four cases
g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-indefinite.emphasisNote: The dative row is this lesson: einem, einem, einer, keinen.
g-daf-a2-inflections-with-the-indefinite.asideNote: The genitive is shown for completeness; it is taught in a later topic.

key.means: ein has no plural, so the plural forms shown are kein- (and mein-, dein- … behave the same way)
the article keinen, and the noun takes an extra -n: keinen Söhnen
the article eines, and the noun takes -s or -es: eines Sohnes

g-daf-a2-personal-pronouns-in-nominative.caption: Personal pronouns
g-daf-a2-personal-pronouns-in-nominative.emphasisNote: The dative column is what this topic adds. uns and euch are the same in the accusative and the dative.

g-daf-a2-adjectives-after-the-definite-a.caption: Adjective ending after der / das / die
g-daf-a2-adjectives-after-the-definite-a.emphasisNote: These five boxes take -e. Everything else takes -en.

key.means: the short ending, e.g. der alte Mann
the long ending, e.g. den alten Mann

g-daf-a2-adjectives-after-ein-kein-mein.caption: Adjective endings after ein- / kein- / mein-
g-daf-a2-adjectives-after-ein-kein-mein.emphasisNote: These three boxes are the whole difference from the der/das/die table. ein does not show the gender, so the adjective does it instead: ein guter Mann, ein gutes Haus.

key.means: the ending der or das would have carried, moved onto the adjective

g-daf-a2-adjectives-before-nouns-without.caption: Adjective endings with no article
g-daf-a2-adjectives-before-nouns-without.emphasisNote: With no article in front, the adjective takes the ending the article would have had: guter Wein, gutes Bier, mit gutem Wein.

key.means: article endings doing duty on the adjective, because there is no article to carry them

g-daf-a1-regular-verbs-in-the-present-te.caption: Present tense: the six endings, and the two spelling rules
g-daf-a1-regular-verbs-in-the-present-te.emphasisNote: The ending column is the pattern: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en. Take the stem (komm-) and add it.

key.means: stem ends in -t or -d, so an extra -e goes in before the ending: du arbeitest, not du arbeitst
stem ends in -ß, -s or -z, so the du-ending loses its -s: du heißt, not du heißst
